resolutions.researcher_notes: Energy Transfer Partners, L.P.'s FY2007 Form 10-K (SEC EDGAR, filed 2007-10-30): 'The Oasis pipeline, a 583-mile natural gas pipeline that directly connects the Waha Hub to the Katy Hub... It has bi-directional capability with approximately 1.2 Bcf/d of throughput capacity moving west-to-east' -- 1.2 Bcf/d = 1,200 MMcf/d, exact match to the sheet's Capacity=1200.00/CapacityUnits=MMcf/d. The company's September 2004 analyst-meeting presentation (filed as Exhibit 99.1 to an 8-K, SEC EDGAR) independently restates 'Oasis Pipeline Capacity of 1.2 Bcf/d' and, in prose, 'Oasis has bi-directional capability with approximately 1 Bcf/d of west-to-east throughput capacity.' Both documents are Energy Transfer's own self-reported figures (one origin, not two independent publishers -- a 10-K and an investor presentation from the same filer), so tier is medium/independent:false, but the two documents, three years apart, agree exactly on the 1,200 MMcf/d design-capacity figure. NOTE: the CURRENT (2023) Energy Transfer operations page describes an expanded system at 'Capacity of 2.0 billion cubic feet per day' -- that is the post-expansion state and does NOT support the sheet's 1200 MMcf/d value, so I have not proposed it for this unit (it may be relevant to a future update of the row's status, not to sourcing the existing figure).

Energy Transfer's September 2004 analyst-meeting presentation (Exhibit 99.1 to an 8-K, SEC EDGAR) states in prose (twice): 'The Oasis Pipeline is a 600 mile, bi-directional pipeline that connects the Waha Hub to the Katy Hub' and 'As of December 2002, ETC owns a 100% interest in the Oasis pipeline, a 600 mile, 24-inch and 36-inch diameter natural gas pipeline that connects the Waha Hub to the Katy Hub.' 600 miles = 965.6 km, matching the sheet's LengthKnown=966.00/LengthKnownUnits=km almost exactly (rounding). Single origin (Energy Transfer itself), so medium/independent:false. CONCERN (informational, not changing the value): the SAME presentation ALSO carries a bullet-point asset summary elsewhere on the same page reading 'Oasis Pipeline ... 583 miles of pipeline,' and Energy Transfer's FY2004 and FY2007 10-Ks (SEC EDGAR) both consistently give the pipeline's length as '583 miles' / '583-mile' rather than 600. So the company's own materials carry two different length figures for the same asset (a rounder '600 mile' marketing description vs. a more precise engineering '583 mile' figure used in its audited 10-K asset table) -- 583 mi = 938.2 km, about 28 km (3%) short of the sheet's 966 km. I am proposing the 600-mile document because it is the closer match and appears to be the actual origin of GEM's figure, but flagging that the company's own more precise (10-K) figure is 583 miles/938 km, in case Baird wants to reconcile to that instead.

Energy Transfer's current operations page (live origin 403s to automated fetchers -- confirmed via curl, not a deletion; Wayback capture from 2023-12-01 is live) states: 'Oasis Pipeline, LP's pipeline system...is primarily a 36-inch diameter, 750 mile, intrastate natural gas pipeline that extends from the Waha Hub market in Pecos County, Texas to the Katy Hub market in Waller County, Texas.' Energy Transfer Partners' FY2007 10-K (SEC EDGAR) independently corroborates the corridor: 'an intrastate pipeline that transports natural gas between the Waha Hub and the Katy Hub near Houston, Texas' and 'The Oasis pipeline, a 583-mile natural gas pipeline that directly connects the Waha Hub to the Katy Hub.' Both endpoints -- Pecos County/Waha in west Texas and Waller County/Katy near Houston in east Texas -- are within the state of Texas, matching the sheet's StartState/Province=Texas and EndState/Province=Texas. Both documents are Energy Transfer's own self-description (one origin), so medium/independent:false, though the corridor identity (Waha to Katy, both Texas) is unchanged across the 2007 filing and the current 2023 marketing page despite the pipeline's length/capacity having grown between those dates via expansion.
